intro.title: Build chaos test for intermittent upstream failures
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a chaos test that simulates intermittent failures in an upstream service, helping you understand how to make your Node.js applications more resilient. You will learn to use a simple Node.js script to randomly introduce errors or delays, mimicking real-world unreliable network conditions. The core programming concept involves using conditional logic and random number generation to control failure simulation. You will work with basic JavaScript constructs like Math.random(), setTimeout(), and error handling to create and run this test.
intro.usecase: Chaos testing for intermittent upstream failures is essential in distributed systems like e-commerce platforms, payment gateways, and API-driven services. Developers implement this pattern to simulate scenarios where third-party APIs, microservices, or databases become temporarily unavailable, ensuring their applications degrade gracefully. For example, an order processing dashboard might use chaos tests to verify it displays helpful error messages and retry options when the payment service flakes out, rather than crashing entirely. This proactive testing helps build resilient systems that maintain core functionality even during partial outages, directly improving user experience and business continuity.
